# SCI-FRUIT scientific-core decision map

Status: sanitized author-input candidate. These rows organize the approved
scope; exact packet approval and launch remain separate.

## Resolved scope direction

The owner approved `SCI-FRUIT-SCIENTIFIC-CORE-SCOPE-R0.1` on 2026-09-06.
The following are restatements of that approved boundary, with scientific
closure delegated only as specified in the Scope Brief.

| Core ID | Direction | Consequence for authorship |
| --- | --- | --- |
| CORE-01 | Author a conditional scientific core, with no numerical profile | Define scientific obligations and conditional properties; do not select or certify a method |
| CORE-02 | Distinguish target sky, map, feedback model and applied model | Require declared scientific compatibility; do not equate them through shared shape or units |
| CORE-03 | Own the feedback composition while retaining adjacent ownership | Describe the declared transition and its input/output/state dependencies; do not redefine PTC, MAP, JINC or NOI |
| CORE-04 | Separate conditional response from adaptive-procedure response | State precisely which operator/state is fixed and which dependence is included; no unconditional derivative or transfer claim |
| CORE-05 | Causal completeness governs continuation | All state that can change future required results matters, regardless of whether it is called a diagnostic |
| CORE-06 | Completion, maximum, convergence, terminal selection and consumer fitness are different claims | Describe their relation and failure/unavailable meanings; invent no numerical stopping or acceptance rule |
| CORE-07 | Conditional scientific verification precedes performance claims | Derive predictive limiting cases with explicit assumptions; do not turn them into observational qualification |
| CORE-08 | The core may be authored before a qualified numerical replacement | This exception applies only to the core; it does not remove later numerical development, qualification or replication requirements |

No new numerical owner decision is supplied by this map. Approval of the
packet would approve these exact restatements and the bounded author task.

## Deferred numerical decisions and their effect on the core

| Decision domain | Remains unselected | Required core treatment |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Recurrence and state representation | Particular transition law, accumulation rule and numerical feedback-state representation | Define a declared stateful operator and its scientific obligations; no default additive law |
| Numerical parent and grouping | MAP/JINC/filter route, observation/coadd composition and numerical admission | Conditional interfaces only; listing a producer does not admit a route |
| Astronomical model | Sky representation, model construction, sign, selection, source profile and physical prior | Require an exact target and compatible model declaration before numerical use; do not choose one |
| Projection and rejoin | Projector, removal/restoration support and downstream response/normalization | Require a declared scientific composition; derive properties only under named assumptions |
| Learning and adaptation | Detector rules, processing policies, fitting populations and adaptive bounds | Bind fixed/learned/applied state and all causal dependencies; no policy recommendation |
| Termination | Thresholds, persistence, resource maximum and terminal selector | Treat them as exact method declarations; lack of a convergence rule prevents a convergence claim |
| Uncertainty and validation | Covariance model, randomization/replay method, population and accuracy criteria | Scope every conditional claim; do not supply a missing distribution or infer numerical adequacy |
| Product use and retention | Consumer acceptance, archive tier and numerical persistence policy | Distinguish identity, causal sufficiency and scientific-use authority |

These are deferred method choices, not all unresolved blockers for a
conditional core. The author must not stop solely because a numerical value
or profile is intentionally unbound. Conversely, a conditional statement that
requires one of these choices must state the condition or remain unavailable.

## Scientific question rule

The manager identifies no additional scope-level numerical choice that must
be made before attempting this core. This is a readiness judgment, not proof
that every derivation will close. If a genuine core-level ambiguity remains,
return the question, the conflicting or missing premises, the narrow candidate
answers and their scientific consequences. Do not decide a physical model or
numerical policy by convenience. Routine notation and equivalent presentation
choices are the author's responsibility.

The author must preserve the distinction between a claim about all declared
methods under a stated assumption and a claim about one numerically realized
method. An existence example or counterexample establishes only its named
mathematical proposition.
